summary: Not a Primal Instinct call. This is a third-party high-ticket sales mastermind run by Josh Lyons, teaching a methodology he calls 'scriptless selling', captured into the Ben Byrne rep folder. No Primal Instinct staff speak at any point and Ben Byrne is never audible, though Josh Lyons is named on two Primal Instinct internal calls this week as someone advising Ben, so attendance is the likely explanation for the recording sitting here. The session is a Q&A following a call review of a member named Annalise. Josh teaches a discovery sequence — surface burning problem, then data collection around it, then impact on other areas of life, then 'why now' — and explicitly applies it to fitness offers. The rest is member questions handled largely through a spiritual frame: no-show rates treated as a spiritual rather than operational problem, self-doubt reframed as an accumulation of untaken physical actions, childhood trauma reframed as irrelevant to the present, and financial scarcity reframed as an internal choice that produces the external result.
notable: The methodology taught here is explicitly anti-script and directly at odds with the scripted Kettlebell Body process the reps are scored against: 'since when was the ultimate way to have freedom... you wanted freedom, and then you decided to have a rigid script. When did control ever turn into freedom?' This is relevant context for the systematic omission of the scripted consequence frame and commitment check across this rep's calls.

Josh's own sequence contains no equivalent of the playbook's Phase 5 or Phase 6 as written: 'what's the surface-level burning problem?... Then I gather all the data around that... I will then usually go into the impact of that thing on other areas of their life... then I would usually go into, so given that this is the issue... why now do you need to do something about it?'

The methodology is taught for fitness offers specifically: 'health offer or fitness. They say that I don't like my body shape... They're not reaching their potential, they don't like the way they look, or they don't like their energy. That's how you then dig into the relevant data.'

Trainer advises against operational fixes for no-show rates in favour of a spiritual explanation: 'I wouldn't incentivize someone... I would challenge you to try and solve this problem spiritually... It's usually a spiritual lesson when our call volume is going up and down and up and down. It's usually not a logical lesson.'

Trainer tells a member disclosing childhood trauma to stop attributing her struggles to it: 'I wouldn't advise you to hold on to the belief that it comes from trauma of your childhood, because that's the same as like the self-doubt being up in your head... the trauma that you lived is in the past, it doesn't exist anymore.'

Trainer tells a financially stressed closer that her lack of money is a reflection of an internal state: 'even if you had a bunch of money in the bank, that's only there because of a reflection of your own internal abundance anyway... If you don't have something outside of you, it's because you don't have it inside of you.'
Trainer advises a member to comply with an employer whose approach she disagrees with rather than raise it: 'your only choice is do what they say or get fired. That's your two options.'
Trainer to a member asking a question before completing the onboarding programme: 'just respectfully sit down, shut up, and do the work.'
Aside during a coaching answer: 'you had the most beautiful girlfriend, unless you're gay and you like guys, so no disrespect there.'

A member describes throwing speculative personal questions at prospects to find leverage: 'sometimes you have to throw like a Hail Mary... do you have a family? And they're like, oh yeah, I've got three kids. And you're like, okay, now it all makes sense', endorsed as 'a few splashes' of intuition.
Contrast with a prior methodology the members name as BBA: 'we would almost like dig, dig, dig, dig, dig until they like told us what we wanted to hear.'

This recording contains the names, business circumstances, financial distress and personal disclosures of at least seven people with no relationship to Primal Instinct, and it is sitting inside a Primal Instinct rep folder being processed as part of a sales-call corpus.
